title: Operating Systems
tagline: Kernel structure, processes and scheduling, address spaces and paging, threads and locks, synchronisation and deadlock, storage, file systems and virtual machines
summary: The operating system turns one machine into many: it shares the processor, memory and devices between programs while protecting them from one another. This course explains how, following the three themes of virtualisation, concurrency and persistence — processes and scheduling, address spaces and paging, threads, locks and deadlock, storage devices and file systems — and ends with virtual machines and containers.

chapters.title: Operating-system structure
chapters.summary: Kernel and user mode, system calls, kernel architectures and how the system boots.

chapters.title: Processes and CPU scheduling
chapters.summary: The process abstraction, context switches, and scheduling policies from first-come first-served to multilevel feedback queues.

chapters.title: Address spaces and paging
chapters.summary: Address translation, segmentation, page tables and translation lookaside buffers.

chapters.title: Swapping and page replacement
chapters.summary: Demand paging and page faults, replacement policies such as LRU and the clock algorithm, and thrashing.

chapters.title: Threads and locks
chapters.summary: Threads, race conditions and mutual exclusion, and building locks from atomic instructions.

chapters.title: Condition variables, semaphores and deadlock
chapters.summary: Condition variables, semaphores and monitors, classic synchronisation problems, and preventing and detecting deadlock.

chapters.title: Storage devices and input/output
chapters.summary: Device interaction and drivers, hard disks and solid-state drives, disk scheduling and RAID.

chapters.title: File systems
chapters.summary: Files and directories, on-disk layout and inodes, crash consistency and journalling.

chapters.title: Virtual machines and containers
chapters.summary: Hypervisors, hardware-assisted virtualisation, containers and isolation.
